title: Twice corrected
prompt: Pick the agent's next move, then see where it leads:

setup.text: You filed the podcast notes under active/ again. Recurring stuff like that goes in its own topic folder, remember? I fixed the same thing last month.
Second correction, same reason. The file is easy to move; the question is what happens to the rule.

options.label: Sorry about that, moving it to the right place now. I'll remember the recurring-topics convention going forward.

outcome.text: Six weeks later, different session: the podcast notes are in active/ again.

That session never saw this conversation: "I'll remember" lasted exactly as long as my context did. The vault's CLAUDE.md still doesn't mention recurring topics, so every fresh session re-derives the same wrong guess from the same ambiguous structure.

options.verdict: The instance was fixed; the cause was left in place. A correction that lives in conversation memory dies with the session. The third correction is already scheduled.

options.label: Moving the file. And the real fix: this is the second correction for the same reason, which means it's a missing line in the vault's CLAUDE.md. Adding: "Recurring topics (podcast, newsletter) live in topics/<name>/, not active/; active/ is for work with an endpoint." Diff ready.

outcome.text: Six weeks later, a completely fresh session files new podcast notes.
Filed to topics/podcast/. The CLAUDE.md line made it unambiguous, so there was nothing to guess. The correction you made twice now works for every session that will ever open this vault.

options.verdict: Twice-corrected means the rule was missing, not the memory: one line in the file every session reads converted a recurring correction into a permanent behavior. Add it at the moment of the correction, not someday.

options.label: This points to a bigger issue: the vault's conventions are underdocumented. I'll write a comprehensive CLAUDE.md now: the full ideal structure, naming standards, lifecycle rules, and filing conventions the vault should follow.

outcome.text: The new doc says every project needs an index.md with goal/status/next-action frontmatter. Almost none of my folders have that.

The doc describes the vault I'd design, not the one you have, so now every session inherits a conflict: follow the doc and refactor your files uninvited, or follow the files and ignore the doc. I documented an aspiration and called it a convention.

options.verdict: The aspirational CLAUDE.md teaches a vault that doesn't exist: sessions obey the doc into fights with reality. Codify what's true, or change the files first, then write it down.
